sovereign_country.strategic_role: 北美成熟市场、联邦与省两级公司实体设立（EPC合规）

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Offshore Trade Intermediary and Commercial Re-Invoicing Operations

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (bijural: civil law for Quebec private law, common law for federal public law)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) between Canada and the European Union
Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP)
Agreement between Canada and the People's Republic of China for the Promotion and Reciprocal Protection of Investments (Canada-China FIPA)
Canada-United States Tax Convention (1980), as amended

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, SC 2000, c 17 (PCMLTFA); Criminal Code, RSC 1985, c C-46 (terrorism financing and structuring); Canada Business Corporations Act, RSC 1985, c C-44, s 21.1 (federal significant-control register, public since 22 January 2024); Quebec Business Corporations Act, CQLR c S-31.1; Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c P-44.1, arts 8.1-8.5 (significant beneficiary disclosure to Registrar); Regulation respecting the register of enterprises, CQLR c P-44.1, r 3; Charter of the French Language, CQLR c C-11; sanctions under Special Economic Measures Act, SC 1992, c 17; Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act (Sergei Magnitsky Law), SC 2017, c 21; United Nations Act, RSC 1985, c U-2.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of passport and national identity card for each director, shareholder, ultimate beneficial owner and senior managing officer
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport authority or civil registration authority of the individual's country of nationality
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if issuing state is Party to the Hague 1961 Convention; otherwise Consular Legalization at the Canadian embassy/consulate with jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency and/or Certificate of Good Standing for any corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign corporate registry or competent company registrar in the shareholder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization as applicable; certificates must be dated not more than 30 days before filing and be apostilled within the 90-day validity window

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney or resolution appointing the Quebec registered agent and process-serve address
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the jurisdiction of execution (Quebec notary for Quebec-origin documents)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for Quebec notarial instruments; foreign execution requires apostille/legalization and certified French or English translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and professional source-of-funds declaration for each funding shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed financial institution holding the account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille/legalization plus notarized signature of bank officer; letter must be current and accompanied by a sworn source-of-funds affidavit

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified translation (French/English) of all non-English or non-French corporate documents
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: OATCCQ-certified translator (Ordre des traducteurs, terminologues et interprètes agréés du Québec) or equivalent court-certified translator in common law provinces
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Translator certification must be notarized; if the translated public document is to be relied upon abroad, attach apostille to the underlying source document

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory FINTRAC-reporting institution screening against: (a) Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) including domestic and foreign PEPs and family/close associates pursuant to PCMLTFA Regulations SOR/2002-184 and SOR/2002-180; (b) United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions list; (c) Canadian Regulations Establishing an Automatic Sanctions List (Special Economic Measures Act and United Nations Act); (d) Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) SDN list for cross-border USD transactions; (e) Global Affairs Canada sanctions list; and (f) domestic terrorism and money-laundering watchlists under the RCMP and Criminal Code. Enhanced due diligence (EDD) triggers on any PEP, high-risk jurisdiction, offshore tax haven, or intermediary nominee structure; independent source-of-funds and source-of-wealth verification required on all UBOs. Ongoing transaction monitoring for unusual or non-economic re-invoicing patterns.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) – Services en ligne, https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca; for federal corporate names via Corporations Canada, https://www.ic.gc.ca/CorporateNameSearch (choice of federal vs Quebec provincial incorporation affects the registry).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Quebec requires every business name to be in French (Charter of the French Language, CQLR c C-11, arts 25-29). A company may also have a version of its name in another language, provided the French version is declared and used in official documents. Non-Latin scripts (e.g., Chinese, Arabic, Cyrillic) must be transliterated into French or English legal characters. The corporate name must not consist solely of a generic term and must be distinctive; the legal element 'Inc.' or 'Corp.' may be used in accordance with the Business Corporations Act. Any English-only designation will be refused unless a recognized trademark exception applies.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If REQ refuses a name reservation, the applicant must file a written request for reconsideration with the Registraire des entreprises within 30 days, stating the grounds for contesting the refusal and submitting corrected supporting reasons. If the Registraire maintains the refusal, an administrative appeal may be brought before the Court of Québec (Civil Division) pursuant to the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c P-44.1, arts 58-60. Alternatively, the applicant may apply for a new reservation with a revised name. For federal CBCA name rejections, the appeal is filed with the Director under s 105 of the Canada Business Corporations Act and ultimately to the Federal Court.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Accepted for incorporation and statutory service address purposes, provided the address is a real physical location in Quebec (not a post-office box) and is staffed by the registered agent during business hours. For the ISIC 4690 re-invoicing/trade intermediary model, a virtual office will create heightened commercial substance risk with the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) and financial institutions; banks and XT/transfer gateways typically require a genuine office, employees, and active management in Quebec to obtain merchant and cross-border processing accounts.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate; estimated 12% annual probability of unannounced inspection or bank/KYC site visit, increasing to 30% for shareholding with foreign PEP involvement or high-risk source jurisdiction. CRA may conduct unannounced GST/QST audit visits; the AMF (Autorité des marchés financiers) and FINTRAC may inspect only where the entity is registered under money-services or securities gateways, which are not triggered by plain wholesale re-invoicing.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Quebec corporate name reservation and priority search (Analyse de nom) at Registraire des entreprises
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff per Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises and REQ fee schedule; CAD 35 converted to USD

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Constitution of Quebec Business Corporation (articles of incorporation) through REQ / notary registration
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory filing fee plus notarial tariff (CAD 300 flat for base constitution in Quebec), excluding ministerial authorization for sensitive words

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office and service agent for statutory notices (annual retainer)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed registered agent / corporate service provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark: CAD 150-300 per annum for Quebec compliance with physical address

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization, apostille and consular legalization bundle for director/UBO identity and corporate documents (5 documents)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary public, Canadian Global Affairs authentication office, relevant consulate
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark: CAD 60-120 per notarization; CAD 25 per apostille authentication; consular fees vary by embassy; includes OATCCQ certified translations

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/UBO background screening, PEP and sanctions database checks for 3 individuals (directors/UBOs)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: External compliance service provider / AML software vendor
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Per-subject screening rate of CAD 50-100 with automated World-Check/Refinitiv or equivalent; plus enhanced due diligence report by outside counsel

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Drafting of corporate by-laws, minutes of initial directors, UBO register and shareholder register
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Quebec legal counsel / corporate law firm
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Blended corporate-law hourly rate of CAD 250-450/hour; estimated 2-3 hours for standard re-invoicing vehicle

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Quebec Business Corporations Act (QBCA), CQLR c. S-31.1, ss. 9-41 (incorporation), ss. 99-147 (management of affairs), ss. 155-170 (by-laws and meetings); alternative federal regime: Canada Business Corporations Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-44, ss. 5-20 and ss. 97-116; legal publicity and registration obligations: Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c. P-44.1, ss. 2-34. The composite jurisdiction CA_QC selects the QBCA as the primary incorporating statute.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) / Quebec Enterprise Registrar, Direction de l'immatriculation; supplemental federal registration with Corporations Canada (Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada) only if the CBCA option is used.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles de constitution / Articles of Incorporation filed electronically through the REQ Secure E-Services module (Dépôt d'actes); the filing must be accompanied by the name reservation certificate and the prescribed constitutive deposit fee, approximately CAD 250 (USD 190), inclusive of the registration entry and issuance of the first certificate of incorporation; the annual declaration duty is charged separately.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies to a QBCA or CBCA business corporation; the subscription price for common shares may be nominal, and no escrow account or capital blocking mechanism is mandated in Quebec for a general re-invoicing trade entity. A majority of the directors must be resident Canadians under QBCA s. 107; non-resident ownership is permitted but triggers enhanced banking AML/KYC information requirements, and any transfer restrictions must be stated in the articles.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: BE IT RESOLVED THAT: (1) The Articles of Incorporation of the Corporation, as attested by the Registraire des entreprises du Québec on [DATE], are hereby ratified and adopted; (2) The subscription for [•] common shares by the incorporator is accepted, and such shares are issued against lawful consideration of $[•] per share, fully paid and non-assessable; (3) The registered office of the Corporation is established at [•], Québec [POSTAL CODE], and such address is designated as its head office; (4) [NAME] and [NAME] are appointed President and Secretary-Treasurer, respectively; (5) The President is authorized to open bank accounts, execute banking resolutions, and file all declarations with the Registraire, Revenu Québec, and the CRA; and (6) A corporate minute book shall be maintained at the registered office. CARRIED.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) - online Name Reservation Service (Nom d'entreprise); NUANS-equivalent search generated through the REQ portal or an accredited agent.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File a name reservation request through the REQ online e-service, providing three ranked name alternatives. The REQ searches its distinctive-name database; a French version of the name is required in Quebec for public documents, and the chosen name must not create confusion with existing registrants or violate public order. The reservation is issued for a statutory validity period, during which the incorporation filing must be completed.
required_dossiers: Name reservation application (online form)
REQ name search certificate (auto-generated NUANS-equivalent report)
Identity of incorporator: full legal name, residential address, date of birth or corporate legal identity
Declaration of the proposed business activity and general objects
Ranked list of three candidate names with French versions
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the REQ refuses or queries the name as confusingly similar, the applicant may file a written explanatory submission or substitute the next ranked name on the same application; a contested name decision may be judicially reviewed before the Superior Court of Quebec within 30 days of notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate lawyer or notary (optional); incorporator acting under the QBCA and the Act to establish a legal framework for information technology, CQLR c. C-1.1.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the articles of incorporation using the REQ template for a share-capital business corporation. The articles must state the corporate name, the head office address (which must be in Quebec), the authorized share structure and classes, any restrictions on share transfers, the number of directors (minimum one), and any limitation on the corporation's business. The incorporator executes the articles; the signature may be electronic. Consents of the initial directors are obtained and annexed.
required_dossiers: Executed Articles of Incorporation (Statuts - société par actions)
Consent of incorporator
Consent of initial directors (Form)
Certificate of name reservation
Declaration of registered office location within Quebec
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the REQ advises of formal defects, the articles may be corrected and resubmitted; where the registrar issues a refusal, the applicant may file a regularization request or appeal to the Administrative Tribunal of Quebec (TAQ) within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Filing of Articles and Obtaining Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) - Dépôt d'actes online filing portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the executed articles electronically through the REQ's act-deposit workflow together with the name reservation certificate and the prescribed fee. The Registrar verifies compliance with the Act respecting legal publicity of enterprises and, upon approval, enters the legal person into the Register of Enterprises and issues the certified attestation of incorporation, which constitutes conclusive evidence of the corporation's existence and legal publicity.
required_dossiers: Electronically filed Articles of Incorporation with electronic signatures
Name reservation certificate
Proof of fee payment
Contact details of the filing agent and incorporator
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the REQ issues a notice of refusal, the applicant will receive the precise statutory reason; the filing may be corrected and re-presented within the cure period, or an opposition/appeal may be filed with the TAQ; if the certificate contains an error, request formal rectification under the publicity statute.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Initial Declaration of Directors and Registered Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) - Déclaration initiale module.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 30 days of incorporation, file the initial declaration setting out the full legal name, residential address, and date of birth of each director, the registered office address, the mailing address, and the principal business activity code. This declaration creates the public record required by the Act respecting legal publicity of enterprises and must be kept current through annual declarations; any subsequent change must be filed within 30 days.
required_dossiers: Signed Déclaration initiale form
Directors' names, residential addresses and dates of birth
Registered office and mailing address in Quebec
ISIC/NAICS activity code for the re-invoicing trade
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late filing penalties are imposed by the REQ; the corporation may file a letter explaining reasonable causes and request a waiver of the late fee; if the registrar initiates cancellation for failure to declare, the corporation may oppose the cancellation within 60 days and regularize the file.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Federal and Provincial Tax Registration (CRA Business Number; Revenu Québec Accounts)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) - Business Registration Online (BRO); Revenu Québec - Inscription des entreprises portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the new corporation with the CRA to obtain a 9-digit Business Number and program accounts: RT (corporation income tax), RP (payroll if any employees), and RM (import/export where applicable). Separately register with Revenu Québec for the Quebec Sales Tax (QST), the corporate income tax file, and other provincial accounts. GST/HST and QST registration is mandatory once taxable revenues exceed the CAD 30,000 small-supplier threshold; registrations should be completed no later than the date the corporation commences commercial activity.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation / REQ attestation
NEQ number (numéro d'entreprise du Québec)
Registered office and mailing address
Directors' and officers' identification data
Description of the re-invoicing business model and anticipated revenue flows
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CRA or Revenu Québec pauses the application for incomplete KYC, the corporation must submit the certified attestation and full identification of the beneficial owners; penalty relief may be requested under the CRA taxpayer relief provisions and the equivalent Revenu Québec statutory relief regime.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Meeting, By-law Adoption, Share Issuance and Minute Book Setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors and corporate secretary; corporate counsel (no REQ filing required for internal by-laws unless they affect public registry particulars).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: At the first meeting of the board, adopt By-Law No. 1 covering director powers, quorum, officers, banking, indemnification and execution of documents; approve the share subscription, issue certificates, and record the share register; appoint officers; adopt a banking resolution designating signatories; and open the corporate bank account. All minutes, registers and the share certificate book are maintained in the minute book at the registered office. A unanimous shareholder agreement, if any, is filed with the REQ only where the parties elect to make it enforceable against third parties.
required_dossiers: Pro-forma first board resolution (as set out above)
By-Law No. 1
Share certificates and securities register
Bank account opening resolution and signatory mandates
Officer appointment consents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Should a title or registry defect be identified, the board may adopt confirmatory resolutions retroactively validating the issuance; failure to maintain the corporate register may lead to a REQ notice of default, which is cured by immediate production of the missing records and, if applicable, restoration of the corporate standing.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable to a pure commercial re-invoicing intermediary under ISIC 4690 / NAICS 425120; no sectoral industrial licence is issued for wholesale trade intermediaries. Conditional authorities include: the local municipal planning department for a business establishment permit, the Régie du bâtiment du Québec (RBQ) for any conversion or structural works, and the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) for an importer/exporter account if physical goods cross the border.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No provincial operating licence is mandated for general re-invoicing operations; a municipal business establishment permit (permis de commerce et d'occupation) is required if a physical office or depot is maintained, and CNESST establishment registration applies where employees are engaged.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP), Direction de l'évaluation environnementale, Quebec
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt / administrative declaration category: an office-based re-invoicing hub does not trigger a mandatory environmental impact assessment under the Environment Quality Act, CQLR c. Q-2. A formal permit under section 22 or section 31 of the EQA becomes mandatory only if the site is converted to warehousing, goods repackaging, or any activity generating effluent, air emissions, or hazardous waste.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: None applicable for administrative re-invoicing operations. Conditional triggers: future warehousing must comply with municipal sewer by-laws and the Regulation respecting municipal wastewater treatment (Règlement sur l'assainissement des eaux); air emissions must respect the Clean Air Regulation (Règlement sur l'assainissement de l'atmosphère, CQLR c. Q-2, r. 4.1); and any hazardous waste handling requires compliance with the Regulation respecting hazardous materials (Règlement sur les matières dangereuses, CQLR c. Q-2, r. 32) and a MELCCFP attestation where applicable.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Office occupancy requires: (i) a fire safety certificate (certificat de sécurité incendie) issued by the local fire prevention service, (ii) an occupancy permit (certificat d'occupation) from the municipality, and (iii) registration of the establishment with the Commission des normes, de l'équité, de la santé et de la sécurité du travail (CNESST) under the Act respecting occupational health and safety, CQLR c. S-2.1. Structural load inspection by a licensed engineer is required only if shelving, racks, or inventory storage is installed; compliance with the Quebec Building Code is mandatory for any leasehold improvements.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA / Agence du revenu du Canada) for federal corporate income tax and GST/HST administration, via the CRA My Business Account portal (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency.html); Revenu Québec (Agence du revenu du Québec) for Quebec corporate income tax and Quebec Sales Tax (QST) administration, via the CliquezAffaires / Mon dossier d'entreprise portal (https://www.revenuquebec.ca/); the Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) independently issues the Quebec Enterprise Number (NEQ).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Incorporate the Business Corporation under the Canada Business Corporations Act or the Quebec Business Corporations Act and register with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec to obtain the NEQ. Step 2: Apply to the CRA for the federal Business Number (BN), which is the statutory TIN for federal tax program accounts (RT corporate tax, RC GST/HST, RP payroll), using Business Registration On-line (BRO) or CRA Form RC1; non-resident applicants use the CRA non-resident registration channel or Form RC171. Step 3: Register for GST/HST under Part IX of the Excise Tax Act once the legal registration threshold is met or when making taxable supplies in Canada. Step 4: Register for QST through Revenu Québec referencing the NEQ; the QST registration number is the NEQ plus a TQ program-account suffix. Step 5: Appoint a service agent in Quebec if required by the enterprise registrar, and maintain books and records at the registered office. Step 6: Validate the entity's banking and remittance identity by linking the Canadian dollar settlement account to the BN such that wire payments (SWIFT M/T, TT, XT-Transfer rails) can be reconciled electronically with GST/QST filings.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no US-style elective check-the-box regime; a CBCA/BCA business corporation is per se an entity-level taxpayer. Substantive elections available to the re-invoicing hub include: (i) associated-corporations allocation election under Income Tax Act (ITA) s.256(2); (ii) initial fiscal-period election permitting a first taxation year of up to 53 weeks under ITA s.249.1; (iii) capital dividend account election under ITA s.83(2) using Form T2054; (iv) ITA s.216 net-basis election for non-resident recipients of Canadian rental or royalty income; (v) hybrid-mismatch elections under ITA s.258(7), with deduction-denial rules under ITA ss.18.4, 18.5 and 258 applying to reverse-hybrid and imported-mismatch structures; and (vi) the closely-related-corporations election under ETA s.238 and QSTA s.499 to treat intra-group supplies as non-taxable for GST/QST.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-added tax: federal Goods and Services Tax (GST) at 5% plus the provincial Quebec Sales Tax (QST) at 9.975% calculated on the GST-inclusive selling price, administered as two separate VATs and reported on separate CRA and Revenu Québec returns
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 in total worldwide taxable supplies, tested over the preceding four consecutive calendar quarters and the current quarter (small-supplier exemption under ETA s.148 and QSTA s.159.1). A re-invoicing hub whose goods are never delivered in Canada may make no Canadian supplies at all and therefore have no registration obligation; a hub holding inventory in Quebec must register when taxable Canadian supplies exceed the threshold. Non-residents soliciting orders in Canada may be deemed registrants irrespective of threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance system, no digital stamping and no mandatory third-party tax clearance API is in force in Canada. Registrants must issue invoices containing the prescribed information set out in ETA s.221(1) and QSTA s.314 (supplier legal name, BN and QST number, invoice date, tax amounts, or a zero-rated notation for exports). Electronic return filing is mandatory for GST/HST and QST registration accounts through CRA NETFILE and Revenu Québec CliquezAffaires. Source records, including EDI or PEPPOL-format e-invoices, SWIFT MT100/MT103 wire messages and bank statements, must be retained for six years.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies under Schedule VI, Part V, ETA where tangible personal property is exported from Canada as soon after the supply as is reasonable and the supplier retains documentary proof of export; it also applies where a non-resident holder of the goods (the offshore principal) instructs shipment from Canada to a destination outside Canada and the hub acts solely as a disclosed agent or title intermediary. If the re-invoiced goods never physically enter Canada, the supply is outside the scope of GST/QST rather than zero-rated. The 0% rate must be claimed at invoicing time; if tax was charged in error, a credit note under ETA s.232 is required before input tax credit refunds are available on the related acquisition costs.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (CBSA Canadian Export Reporting System / CAED report or Form A666 for goods exceeding CAD 2,000)
Bill of Lading (ocean), Air Waybill (air), or cargo manifest / truck carrier CIQI export report (land)
Inward Remittance Certificate / SWIFT MT103 or TT wire proof of foreign currency repatriation
Commercial invoice and purchase-ordre chain evidencing the re-invoicing flow and legal title transfer
Packing list, customs broker summary, and non-resident consignee declaration
Signed zero-rated export-evidence register maintained by the hub, carrier and customs broker
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export substantiation documents must be retained for six years (ETA s.286; ITA s.230). The CRA and Revenu Québec may reassess within four years of the return date (ETA s.298; ITA s.152(4)); the limitation period is unlimited in cases of misrepresentation, fraud or wilful default. An overstated export refund or input tax credit claim attracts a 25% penalty under ETA s.286.1, increased to 50% for a repeat claim within five years, plus a 25% false-document penalty under ETA s.285.1 and, where income tax is affected, a 50% gross-negligence penalty under ITA s.163(2). Erroneously refunded amounts are clawed back retroactively with statutory interest (ETA ss.295, 298). Criminal prosecution under ETA s.328 can result in fines of up to 200% of the tax evaded and imprisonment. Revenu Québec applies mirror penalties and unlimited clawback under the Tax Administration Act (ss.57, 59, 520.1) for QST fraud. In a re-invoicing trade audit, the tax authority will require the hub to reconcile each SWIFT MT103, TT wire or XT-Forex settlement receipt to a specific export declaration and bill of lading; unreconciled foreign currency receipts are recharacterized as taxable Canadian sales, assessed GST/QST on the gross invoice value, and subjected to penalties and interest.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada. Canada has no general foreign-exchange administration imposing exchange controls. The Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions supervises federally regulated deposit-taking institutions; the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada administers anti-money-laundering and terrorist-financing reporting obligations; the Canada Border Services Agency and Canada Revenue Agency administer relevant customs, tax, trade-reporting, and transfer-pricing requirements. In Quebec, the Autorité des marchés financiers regulates applicable securities, derivatives, and financial-market activities.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar is freely convertible for ordinary commercial and financial transactions. Canada generally permits unrestricted current-account payments, including payment for imports, services, royalties, interest, dividends, and repatriation of lawful profits, subject to applicable tax withholding, corporate-law solvency requirements, sanctions, anti-money-laundering controls, contractual restrictions, and bank transaction monitoring. Capital-account transactions, foreign ownership, intercompany financing, acquisitions, securities activities, and derivatives are not subject to general exchange controls but may trigger beneficial-ownership, source-of-funds, sanctions, tax, transfer-pricing, securities, competition, or foreign-investment review. A Quebec corporation should maintain board-approved dividend or capital-return resolutions, evidence of distributable capacity, tax-clearance analysis, intercompany agreements, arm's-length pricing support, and payment records. Non-resident shareholders may generally receive dividends, interest, loan repayments, and other lawful distributions, subject to Canadian withholding tax and any treaty reduction. Canadian banks may request invoices, contracts, customs records, tax forms, ownership evidence, and economic-purpose explanations before releasing or converting funds.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada has no general statutory requirement to surrender export proceeds to a domestic bank, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no universal statutory deadline for converting foreign-currency export receipts. Export proceeds may generally be retained in foreign-currency accounts or converted at the holder's discretion, subject to contractual banking terms, sanctions, anti-money-laundering controls, accounting requirements, tax reporting, customs documentation, and accurate revenue recognition. Financial institutions must comply with applicable suspicious-transaction, large-cash, electronic-funds-transfer, sanctions, and record-keeping obligations. Businesses should reconcile export invoices, shipping or delivery evidence, customs filings where applicable, foreign-currency balances, intercompany pricing, and tax reporting. The absence of surrender controls does not eliminate Canadian income-tax, GST/HST, transfer-pricing, customs-valuation, or beneficial-ownership obligations.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Contribution Account or segregated operating sub-account
Capital Contribution Account or segregated operating sub-account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium for payment operations and low to medium as a substitute for a Canadian operating bank. An offshore electronic-money institution may process lawful cross-border payments only within the permissions of its home-country licence and correspondent or partner-bank arrangements. It cannot automatically provide Canadian deposit-taking, Canadian payment-account, trust, foreign-exchange, or money-services functionality. Canadian counterparties may reject offshore EMI accounts where the account holder, payer, beneficiary, underlying goods, or transaction purpose cannot be independently verified. Use of an offshore EMI does not remove obligations under Canadian anti-money-laundering, sanctions, tax, customs, transfer-pricing, record-retention, payment-transparency, or Quebec consumer and financial-market laws. The corporation should use a Canadian-chartered bank for core collections, payroll, tax payments, customer due diligence, and material trade settlements, with an EMI limited to documented ancillary corridors and subject to transaction limits, reconciliation, segregation, and contingency controls.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical attendance by directors is not generally mandated by Canadian corporate or foreign-exchange law. Remote onboarding may be available at the institution's discretion, subject to reliable identity verification, beneficial-owner verification, corporate-document authentication, sanctions screening, source-of-funds review, and a satisfactory explanation of the business model. Banks may require an in-person meeting, video interview, Canadian authorized signing officer, notarized or certified documents, Canadian address evidence, or a branch visit where ownership is foreign, the business is newly incorporated, activity is cross-border, the entity is a re-invoicing hub, or transaction risk is elevated. A Quebec entity should confirm requirements directly with each bank before incorporation, particularly where no Canadian-resident director, office, operating history, or local personnel exists.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign-owned newly incorporated corporation with no Canadian operating history, employees, premises, or local management.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate and articles of incorporation; Quebec enterprise registration and applicable federal filings; registers of directors, officers, shareholders, and ultimate beneficial owners; organizational chart; board resolutions; Canadian registered-office and operating-address evidence; director and beneficial-owner identification; detailed business plan; management biographies; expected countries, counterparties, currencies, volumes, and payment corridors; initial capitalization evidence; service-provider and logistics arrangements; and a written rationale for the Quebec location.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Commercial re-invoicing or offshore trade-intermediary model with goods moving between third countries and limited Canadian physical activity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: End-to-end transaction-flow memorandum; purchase and resale contracts; invoices; bills of lading; certificates of origin where applicable; customs declarations; proof of delivery; insurance records; pricing and margin policy; transfer-pricing analysis; beneficial-owner and counterparty files; sanctions and restricted-party screening results; description of title passage and risk transfer; expected payment waterfall; and reconciliation procedures demonstrating genuine goods or services and absence of circular payments.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-value or unusual inbound capital contribution, shareholder loan, or intercompany transfer.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed subscription, contribution, or loan agreement; board and shareholder approvals; lender or investor ownership evidence; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds documents; audited or management financial statements; bank statements; tax returns where appropriate; beneficial-owner declarations; repayment and interest terms; transfer-pricing support; sanctions screening; payment purpose narrative; and evidence that the funds are not third-party pass-through proceeds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payments involving jurisdictions, banks, goods, vessels, or counterparties associated with sanctions, export controls, proliferation, corruption, or elevated money-laundering risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Counterparty ownership and control profile; screening reports against Canadian and applicable foreign sanctions lists; end-use and end-user certificates; export-control classification; shipping route and vessel information; licenses or permits; contract and invoice package; compliance approval record; adverse-media review; enhanced due-diligence questionnaire; and documented escalation decision. Do not process a transaction where a prohibition applies or required authorization is absent.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inconsistent transaction volumes, rapid pass-through of funds, payments unrelated to stated NAICS or ISIC activities, or unexplained third-party payments.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Rolling 12-month cash-flow forecast; customer and supplier concentration report; transaction-level invoice register; contract-to-cash reconciliation; explanation of seasonality and trade cycles; approval matrix; segregation-of-duties policy; payment authorization logs; source-and-use-of-funds schedule; bank reconciliation; and independent accounting or audit support.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of offshore EMI, virtual-asset service, payment intermediary, or nested correspondent relationship.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provider licence and regulatory status; ownership and management profile; correspondent-bank information; safeguarding or segregation terms; AML program summary; sanctions controls; transaction limits; settlement and chargeback terms; full funds-flow diagram; counterparty onboarding policy; reconciliation reports; and written explanation of why a Canadian bank is not being used for the relevant corridor.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear ultimate beneficial ownership, nominee arrangements, bearer-like ownership features, trusts, or layered holding companies.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified ownership chain to each natural person exercising control or owning the relevant threshold; shareholder agreements; trust deeds and trustee or protector details where applicable; control-rights analysis; passports and residential-address evidence; corporate registry extracts; tax-residency self-certifications; politically exposed person screening; and signed beneficial-ownership certification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign-exchange conversion or derivative request unsupported by commercial exposure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Underlying invoices and forecast exposures; currency and maturity schedule; hedging policy; board-approved limits; counterparty confirmations; hedge-accounting analysis where used; derivative suitability and appropriateness records; collateral and credit-support documentation; and evidence that the transaction is not speculative or intended to evade reporting or sanctions controls.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route capital through a Canadian-chartered bank account held in the corporation's legal name. Use a bank wire through SWIFT, or an approved domestic clearing route where the remitter and beneficiary institutions support it. The remitter should state the legally accurate purpose, such as equity subscription, shareholder capital contribution, intercompany loan, or trade-finance funding; Canada does not impose a universal foreign-exchange purpose-code system for ordinary corporate wires. Do not label a loan as equity or a commercial payment as capital. Provide the bank with the executed subscription or loan agreement, board approvals, investor or lender ownership information, source-of-funds evidence, expected amount and currency, repayment or dividend terms, tax analysis, and ultimate-beneficial-owner information before remittance. Confirm whether the bank requires an advance incoming-wire notice, foreign-currency account, correspondent-bank details, or supporting documents. Record the exchange rate, value date, fees, accounting treatment, and intercompany balance. Large electronic transfers, suspicious transactions, sanctions concerns, and other reportable events may be subject to Canadian regulatory reporting by the financial institution. Avoid personal accounts, unexplained third-party remitters, split payments, cash funding, and circular transfers.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use Canadian-dollar or foreign-currency operating accounts with dual authorization, beneficiary validation, invoice matching, sanctions screening, and transaction-level reconciliation. For ordinary supplier payments, use SWIFT customer credit transfer, commonly evidenced by an MT103 or its ISO 20022 successor message, subject to the sending and receiving banks' current messaging formats. For documentary trade, use a commercial letter of credit issued or confirmed by a reputable bank, with documentary examination against the credit terms and applicable international rules such as UCP 600 where incorporated. Use documentary collections, open-account wires, or supply-chain finance only after counterparty and goods verification. Maintain purchase contracts, commercial invoices, transport documents, customs records, certificates, insurance documents, proof of delivery, and payment approvals. Canada has no general capital-control requirement to obtain central-bank approval for ordinary import payments, but sanctions, export controls, customs valuation, tax, anti-bribery, anti-money-laundering, and bank-risk controls remain applicable. Establish maker-checker controls, approved beneficiary master data, callback verification for changes, payment limits, positive pay or equivalent fraud controls, and daily liquidity reporting. XT or proprietary transfer labels should be used only where supported by the relevant bank or payment provider and should not replace legally accurate payment narratives or required traceability.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable foreign-exchange forwards with a Canadian bank or appropriately regulated dealer, supported by identified or reasonably forecast commercial exposures and documented counterparty credit limits.

Non-deliverable forwards where permitted by the relevant dealer, applicable law, and transaction documentation. NDF settlement should be limited to genuine currency exposure, with benchmark, fixing, net-settlement, collateral, close-out, and reporting terms clearly documented.

Currency swaps and cross-currency interest-rate swaps for documented funding, liquidity, or currency exposures, subject to dealer eligibility, ISDA or equivalent documentation, collateral terms, valuation controls, and applicable derivatives reporting or clearing obligations.

Foreign-exchange options, collars, and structured hedges only after assessing suitability, premium or collateral requirements, potential leveraged outcomes, accounting treatment, and applicable Quebec and Canadian derivatives rules.

Spot foreign-exchange conversions for settlement and working-capital needs. Maintain a treasury policy prohibiting unsupported speculative positions, setting tenor and notional limits, requiring independent valuation, and requiring board or treasury-committee approval for material derivatives.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 calendar days after each registration anniversary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing incurs monetary penalties and interest; failure to file for two consecutive years may result in administrative deregistration and strike-off of the corporation from the Quebec enterprise register.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal Annual Return (CBCA) — if the corporation is incorporated federally
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada (Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days of the corporation's anniversary date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing can lead to administrative dissolution by Corporations Canada after one year of continued default, with restoration requiring court orders and additional fees.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Canadian federal and Quebec corporate income tax returns (T2 and CO-17)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) and Revenu Québec
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before six months after the taxation year-end; for a December 31 year-end, filing due by June 30
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of the unpaid balance plus 1% per month up to 12 months, on the federal side, with equivalent provincial penalties and interest accruing from the balance-due date.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No audit is compulsory based purely on revenue for a private non-distributing business corporation. An independent audit is mandatory for a distributing corporation (reporting issuer). A non-distributing corporation may dispense with the appointment of an auditor only by unanimous shareholder consent; otherwise shareholders may requisition an audit under the CBCA / Quebec Business Corporations Act.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Financial statements must be prepared in accordance with Canadian GAAP — IFRS for publicly accountable enterprises; for private corporations, either IFRS or Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) may be adopted. Tax filings are reconciled to GAAP with prescribed statutory and tax adjustments.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Federal and Quebec corporate law require continuous maintenance of registers of members, directors, officers, and significant control persons. Under the CBCA, individuals with significant control must be recorded, and any change in significant control must be noted within 15 days of knowledge. The federal and Quebec annual declarations/returns confirm current directors, officers, and registered data. Shareholder transfers must be evidenced in the register of members and reflected in the next annual filing; failure to update registers exposes the corporation to civil penalties.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Significant Control (individuals with significant control)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 26.5% combined general rate (federal Part I 15% + Quebec 11.5%); a Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) resident in Quebec with active business income not exceeding CAD 500,000 may access the Small Business Deduction, producing a combined effective rate of approximately 12.2% (federal 9% + Quebec 3.2%).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Federal Small Business Deduction on first CAD 500,000 of active business income; federal Manufacturing and Processing Profits Deduction reducing federal rate to 13%; federal Scientific Research and Experimental Development (SR&ED) investment tax credit (15% base, 35% refundable for qualifying small CCPCs with legislative phase-down effective 2024-2026); Quebec SR&ED refundable credit at 14%; Quebec innovation and productivity tax credits for manufacturing and green investments; general loss carryback of 3 years. Re-invoicing trade margins are ordinary active business income eligible for the SBD where the entity is a CCPC with worldwide taxable capital under CAD 15,000,000 and passive income limits respected.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return — transmitted to the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) via EFILE or NETFILE through Certified Software Provider portals; CRA payslip remittance via My Payment or financial institution; Quebec coordinates single-window filing through Revenu Québec for tax administrations where the only provincial nexus is Quebec.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual for each taxation year; no quarterly corporation tax return, but quarterly/monthly corporate tax instalments are required where Part I tax exceeds CAD 3,000 for the year.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due within 6 months after the end of the taxation year (e.g., December 31 year-end = June 30 filing deadline). Balance-due date is 2 months after year-end, extended to 3 months for a CCPC resident in Canada throughout the year with taxable income not exceeding CAD 500,000 and aggregate investment income not exceeding CAD 50,000.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, trade names, Business Number (BN), mailing address, provincial registration, language of correspondence, fiscal year-end, type of business activity (NAICS/ISIC mapped to wholesale trade), director names and addresses, Canadian and foreign address fields unlock anti-money-laundering and foreign asset declarations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident-owned corporations file the same T2 but must identify the non-resident owner, indicate the foreign address jurisdiction, attach Form T183 for EFILE authorization where applicable, and prepare a certified copy of the certificate of residence for any treaty-based profit attribution claim.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Line 100 gross revenue from wholesale resale; line 8290 purchases and cost of goods sold, including intercompany inventory purchases; line 8451 amortization and capital cost allowance (from Schedule 7); lines 8710 and 8800 general and administrative expenses; full reconciliation of IFRS/ASPE accounting net income to Part I net income is recorded in Section 5. Re-invoicing hubs must disclose intercompany gross margin benchmarks and retain TP documentation supporting the resale price method.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign-owned re-invoicing corporations must book intercompany purchases to the foreign principal at arm's-length prices; margin erosion achieved through artificial purchasing structures is reported here and triggers Form T106 disclosure and s.247 transfer pricing reassessment risk.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Line 500 taxable income; base Part I tax at 15%; deduction for the Small Business Deduction (Line 533) on active business income up to CAD 500,000; general rate reduction for M&P income; Schedule 21 foreign tax credits and Schedule 31 investment tax credits offset; Part IV tax on dividends and refundable dividend tax on investment income must be computed where the entity holds portfolio investments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders cannot claim the SBD unless the corporation is a CCPC; treaty-based reduction of Canadian tax on business profits requires a permanent establishment attribution analysis; if the Quebec hub is found to lack substance, CRA may impute profits to the foreign principal under Article 7 of Canada's tax treaties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computes Quebec provincial tax using Canadian federal taxable income as the starting point and applies Quebec-specific adjustments; 11.5% general rate or 3.2% reduced rate for eligible SME active business income; Quebec tax credits and deductions, including the Quebec foreign tax credit, are claimed directly on CO-17.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign-resident-owned corporations must file CO-17 if the corporation has a Quebec permanent establishment; the Quebec abatement ensures no double federal-tax provincial overlap; treaty relief does not eliminate Quebec provincial tax absent specific DTA provisions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computes depreciable capital cost by class; class 8 at 20% for office furniture and equipment; class 10 at 30% for vehicles; class 14.1 at 5% for intangible and intellectual property; immediate expensing of qualifying manufacturing and processing machinery in certain conditions; recapture and terminal loss mechanics apply on disposition of re-invoicing assets.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Re-invoicing hubs holding no fixed assets in Quebec should report no CCA; off-balance-sheet warehouse and logistics arrangements involving foreign assets create permanent establishment exposure under OECD attribution rules and must be disclosed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form T106 - Information Return of Non-Arm's Length Transactions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reports every transaction between the Quebec corporation and non-resident related persons where aggregate same-category transfers exceed CAD 1,000,000 or a loan/indebtedness exceeds CAD 50,000; includes Schedule G transfer-pricing method selection, comparability data, and supporting economic analysis.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Canadian filer must identify the non-resident parent, classify transactions by type (inventory resale, services, royalty, interest), and attach the contemporaneous transfer pricing study; failure to file T106 eliminates penalty-relief protection under s.247(3).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late/omitted filing: 5% of balance owing plus 1% per full month up to 12 months; repeated failure (assessed more than once): 10% plus 2% per full month up to 20 months; failure to file Form T106: CAD 25 per day up to CAD 2,500; false or deliberately misleading statements: civil penalty of 50% of the understated Part I tax under s.163(2) plus interest; failure to file for more than 3 years triggers CRA reassessment of the full 3-year normal period being extended by 3 more years (s.152(4)) plus gross-negligence penalties; Quebec CO-17 mirrors the federal late-filing 5%/1% structure with its own interest regime and a 10% repeat-filer penalty.
